articles.title: What Is a Nomogram and Why Would It Interest Me?
articles.originalTitle: What Is a Nomogram and Why Would It Interest Me?
articles.excerpt: A nomogram or nomograph is a diagram that provides an easy, graphical way of calculating the result of a mathematical formula. Sometimes also called an alignment chart, a nomogram consists of a set of numbered scales, usually one for each variable in the formula, arranged so that a straightedge can be placed across known values to find the unknown value that solves the formula. Since an equation in two variables is usually represented by a graph, most nomograms represent formulas that involve three or more variables.

articles.title: Researchers discover why fructose doesn't satisfy hunger like glucose
articles.originalTitle: Researchers discover why fructose doesn't satisfy hunger like glucose
articles.excerpt: A new study found that fructose and glucose may look the same on a nutrition label, but the brain treats them very differently. In mice, glucose strongly reduced activity in hunger-promoting brain cells, while fructose had a much weaker effect. High-fructose corn syrup triggered a stronger response and was preferred by the animals. The findings suggest that the type of sugar—not just the calories—can influence appetite and food preferences.
